# The dense tour counts every root `state.Provider`, so the topology Group's history Provider reads as a second one

> **CORRECTED 2026-09-14 after a captured construction stack refuted this ticket's own premise.** The
> title and the original body claimed a Provider "bound to nothing". It is bound to a Group. The
> correction is kept in place rather than rewritten away, because the wrong reasoning is the useful part.

## Context

`WorkstationNL › the real tour keeps density, data, Canvas output, themes, rails, and identities live`
fails at its very first identity assertion:

```
Error: Workstation owns one root StateProvider
Expected: 1
Received: 2
```

This red rode #17844's census for several runs recorded as "flagged to #18461" and read as owned.
#18461 has since closed without touching it, so that pointer was dead and the red had no open owner.
This ticket is that owner. The census body has been corrected.

## What it actually is

`Neo.manager.Transaction#getProvider` (`src/manager/Transaction.mjs:537`) creates **one `state.Provider`
per Group, on first read** — deliberately parent-less and component-less — so a popped-out window and
its opener read the same `canUndo` / `canRedo` answer. `retireGroup` destroys it with the Group
(`:915`). It is a legitimate second root.

The Workstation reaches it at boot because the topology bar's undo/redo carry history badges
(#18560); `TopologyToolbar.historyStepBadge` calls `getProvider` inside a binding formula, and #18677
only moved that binding into its own view.

**How that was established, since the first answer here was wrong.** A temporary warn in
`Provider#construct`, firing for any instance built with neither `component` nor `parent`, named the
creator:

```
Provider.construct                src/state/Provider.mjs
Object.create                     src/Neo.mjs
Transaction.getProvider           src/manager/Transaction.mjs:537
TopologyToolbar.historyStepBadge  apps/workstation/view/TopologyToolbar.mjs:98
```

and `TransactionManager.getProvider(workspace.topologyGroupId).id` then resolved to that exact
instance, `neo-state-provider-2`.

## The refuted hypothesis, kept

The original body argued the orphan was very likely a **destroyed** Provider still registered: a probe
had returned its `id` and apparently nothing else, which is `core.Base#destroy`'s exact fingerprint
(`_id` survives the delete loop). Two things were wrong with it.

- The reasoning was a reconstruction from reading `destroy`, `afterSetId` and `beforeSetStateProvider`
  — and a reconstruction cannot refute the hypothesis it was built from. The stack could, and did.
- The discriminator did not discriminate. `isDestroyed` reads `undefined` on the two **healthy**
  Providers too, so its absence on the orphan was never evidence of anything. Asserting from it would
  have been a control on the wrong axis.

There is no leak and no engine defect here. `Neo.manager.Transaction` is correct as written.

## The Fix

The arm is what is wrong: it counts roots globally and assumes only the view tree makes them.

1. Count the root Providers that **own a component** — one, the workspace's, which is what the
   identity snapshot means — instead of every parent-less instance.
2. Name the component-less root **by id, from the manager**, rather than relaxing the count to 2.

## Two reds were hiding behind it

The count aborted the arm at `:664`, so nothing downstream of it had a run for as long as #18560 has
been in. Both are newly *visible*, not newly broken:

- `:876` `shortGeometry.scale.height >= 230` — **in scope here**, because it is the same defect shape
  (an assertion stating what the composition does not owe) and it sits between `:664` and any receipt
  that the repair holds. At a 600-tall viewport every band keeps its rem floor — asserted two lines
  above — so the center absorbs the whole block-size delta: the grid goes 516 → 216 for a 300-pixel
  shorter host. Paying 230 out of 216 requires pushing the bottom band under that floor. The two
  assertions cannot both hold.
- `:1266` the dark-mode splitter's `element.matches(':active')` after `mouse.down()` — **out of scope,
  noted in #17844.** Independent of this ticket's subject, unowned, and mode-independent (it fails
  headed and headless alike, so it is not the #18687 shape). Possibly the same ground as #17889.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 The dense tour's root-Provider assertion passes against a booted Workstation, by counting
      component-owning roots — not by relaxing the expected count.
- [ ] AC-2 A component-less root is asserted **by identity**: the arm resolves the topology Group's
      history Provider from `Neo.manager.Transaction` and requires it to be exactly the set of
      component-less roots. A second, unexplained one still fails the arm.
- [ ] AC-3 `shortGeometry.scale.height` is asserted as the viewport-delta relation it actually is, with
      a floor that can hold at 600 CSS pixels.
- [ ] AC-4 Both repaired assertions behave identically headed and headless.
- [ ] AC-5 #17844's census records this arm's disposition and carries `:1266` forward as an attributed,
      unowned red.

## Out of Scope

- `:1266`, and every other red in #17844.
- Any change to `Neo.manager.Transaction`, which this ticket set out to fix and should not touch.
- Whether the arm should count roots at all. It should; the count is what surfaced all of this.

## Related

- #17844 — the census carrying this red, corrected to show it unowned rather than flagged to a closed ticket.
- #18461 — closed; was cited as this red's owner and never touched it.
- #18560 — gave the topology bar its history badges, and with them the second root at boot.
- #18677 — moved that binding into `TopologyToolbar`; not the cause.
- #17889 — pointer-capture migration, a candidate ground for `:1266`.
